category.name: Cloud Security
category.description: Infrastructure threat modeling: identity, network boundaries, secrets, supply chain and blast radius.

lab.title: Serverless Data Lake
lab.summary: An event-driven analytics pipeline built from object storage, functions and a query engine.
lab.businessContext: A media company is building an analytics lake so product teams can query user behaviour data themselves.
lab.systemContext: Client events land in an ingest bucket, a function transforms them into a curated bucket, a query engine serves analysts, and a scheduled job exports aggregates to a partner.

architectureIssues.title: Clients write directly into the ingest bucket
architectureIssues.description: Applications hold credentials that write straight to object storage with no described validation, quota or per-client scoping.
architectureIssues.hint: What else can a leaked client credential do to that bucket?

architectureIssues.title: Transform function has broad storage permissions
architectureIssues.description: The function's role is not scoped to the two buckets it needs, so a compromise reaches far more than the pipeline.
architectureIssues.hint: What is the smallest set of permissions this function actually needs?

architectureIssues.title: Raw user identifiers persist into the curated layer
architectureIssues.description: No pseudonymisation happens during transform, so every analyst query runs against directly identifiable behaviour.
architectureIssues.hint: Does behavioural analysis need to know exactly who?

architectureIssues.title: Analysts query the full curated dataset with no column restrictions
architectureIssues.description: Nothing describes column-level or row-level access control on the query engine.
architectureIssues.hint: Should every analyst see every field?

architectureIssues.title: Partner export has no described integrity or scope check
architectureIssues.description: A scheduled job pushes extracts to a partner endpoint with no stated verification of what is included.
architectureIssues.hint: How would anyone notice if the export started including a raw column?

threats.title: Leaked client credential exposes or poisons the ingest bucket
threats.description: A credential extracted from a mobile app grants direct object storage access, allowing an attacker to read other clients' raw events or flood the bucket.
threats.learnerExplanation: Credentials shipped to clients should be assumed public.

threats.title: Analyst reads identifiable behaviour beyond their need
threats.description: Unrestricted query access over identifiable data means any analyst — or anyone who phishes one — can profile individual users.
threats.learnerExplanation: Self-service analytics multiplies the number of people holding sensitive data.

threats.title: Compromised transform function reaches unrelated storage
threats.description: An overprivileged execution role turns a bug in the transform code into access across the cloud account.
threats.learnerExplanation: Least privilege is what turns a compromise into an incident instead of a breach.

threats.title: Scheduled export silently widens to include personal data
threats.description: With no scope verification, a schema change quietly sends identifiable columns to an external partner.
threats.learnerExplanation: Automated exports drift; nobody reads them after week one.

threats.title: Event flooding drives unbounded storage and compute cost
threats.description: With no quota, an attacker or a buggy client can trigger the transform function millions of times.
threats.learnerExplanation: In serverless the availability risk usually shows up as a bill.

mitigations.title: Ingest through an authenticated API, not direct storage
mitigations.description: Put a validating endpoint in front of the bucket so clients never hold storage credentials.

mitigations.title: Least-privilege role scoped to the two buckets
mitigations.description: Restrict the function's execution role to the specific prefixes and actions it needs.

mitigations.title: Pseudonymise identifiers during transform
mitigations.description: Replace user identifiers with per-dataset tokens so curated data is not directly identifiable.

mitigations.title: Column and row-level access control in the query engine
mitigations.description: Grant analysts only the fields their role requires and log what they query.

mitigations.title: Schema contract and review on the partner export
mitigations.description: Pin the exported columns, fail the job on drift, and alert on any change.

mitigations.title: Enable object versioning on the buckets
mitigations.description: Helps recover from accidental deletion; it does not restrict who can read or write.

mitigations.title: Enable default encryption at rest
mitigations.description: Baseline hygiene that is almost certainly already on and addresses none of these threats.

threatMitigations.explanation: Clients holding no storage credential cannot leak one.
Field-level grants limit what any single analyst can reach.
A narrowly scoped role keeps a code bug inside the pipeline.
A pinned schema that fails on drift catches the silent widening.
An authenticated ingest endpoint is also where quotas and rate limits belong.

releaseGuidance.rationale: One critical issue — client applications holding direct object storage credentials — must be closed before any real traffic, because those credentials should be assumed public the moment the app ships. Everything else is contained and can be sequenced: the pipeline itself is well-shaped, the trust boundaries are sensible, and no single remaining finding causes irreversible harm. This is a reasonable candidate for a conditional launch with an internal-only dataset while the ingest path is replaced.
suggestedConditions: Replace direct client writes with an authenticated ingest API before any production traffic.
Scope the transform function's execution role to the two buckets it uses.
Apply column-level access control before opening self-service queries to analysts.
Pin the partner export schema and alert on drift.
